sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Hong Kong SAR-France Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (1995)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier, Articles L561-1 to L561-45 and R561-1 et seq. (AML/CFT obligations); Code de commerce, Article L561-46 (register of beneficial owners); Décret n°2016-862 du 29 juin 2016 (RBE / UBO register); French Ministerial Order of 12 October 2018 (UBO filing content).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incumbency of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry or Companies House in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the passport of each UBO and proposed manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or consular officer in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille, or consular legalization where the apostille is not accepted

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds statement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Primary issuing bank of the shareholder or UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy plus Hague Apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn French translation of all foreign-language corporate and identity documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Court-appointed expert translator (traducteur agréé près une cour d'appel)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic legalization; no apostille required but the sworn translation must be attached to the apostilled original

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory documentary screening of all shareholders, UBOs, managers, and bank signatories against the EU consolidated financial sanctions lists, UN Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN list where USD clearing is involved, and French FIU (Tracfin) typologies. Persons identified as politically exposed persons (PEPs) must undergo enhanced due diligence with senior-management approval; screen results are archived in the AML/KYC file for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); availability search via INPI Data (data.inpi.fr) and Infogreffe (infogreffe.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be composed in Latin characters; foreign words must be accompanied by a French translation in the registration form and in the compulsory legal publication. The name must not infringe prior registered trademarks, be contrary to public policy, or mislead the public as to the nature of the business.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name pre-emption with INPI lasts 70 days and may be restarted by filing a new application. If the company registry (Greffe) rejects the proposed name, the applicant must obtain the written ground of rejection and may either resubmit a corrected name through the Guichet Unique or file an administrative appeal before the competent supervisory court (Tribunal Judiciaire / Tribunal de Commerce) within 30 days of rejection, seeking an order to compel registration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is permissible for a B2B SaaS SARL when arranged through a licensed professional domiciliation company providing a physical address, mail forwarding, and access to statutory records. Co-working and shared-office arrangements are also accepted, but a bare PO box is not sufficient as a registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low_2_to_5_percent_annual_baseline; the risk rises to 15-20 percent if the domiciliation provider is under administrative supervision or if available tax or payroll filings indicate a lack of commercial substance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: INPI name pre-emption and availability search
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fixed fee approximately EUR 22 plus taxes

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal drafting of articles of association and pre-incorporation due diligence advice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark fixed fee for standard single-member SAS / SARL formation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation notice in a Journal d'Annonces Légales
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-line statutory tariff and newspaper schedule; estimate for a concise notice

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce compétent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official tariff for registry rights and emoluments

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office domiciliation agreement, first annual period
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate for virtual office address with mail handling and statutory-address services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization of foreign corporate and identity documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent foreign authorities and French consular services
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official per-document apostille fees plus consular processing fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn French translation and notarization of certified copies
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-page statutory tariff and notary tariff for certification of copies

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Title III: Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10, L.223-1 to L.223-54, L.223-7 (capital deposit), R.210-2 et seq. (publication formalities), and Decree No. 2022-1258 (Guichet unique digital filing).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS) kept at the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; online filing through the Guichet unique operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Formulaire M0 – Extrait de demande d'immatriculation au Registre national des entreprises (RNE), accompanied by the authenticated Statuts.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for SARL under French law; the articles of association freely determine the capital. Cash contributions must be paid up to at least 20% at incorporation, with the balance payable within five years. Cash funds must be deposited in a French bank account, with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, or with a notary until registration. In-kind contributions must be fully paid-up at subscription and require a Commissaire aux Apports review if valued above €30,000 or where statutory valuation rules apply.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At [date], the founders and future shareholders, acting as the corporate governance body, unanimously resolve as follows. The share subscription of [€X] is approved and the minimum 20% paid-up portion is acknowledged as legally deposited. The registered office is established and maintained at [Address] for all administrative and fiscal purposes. [Name] is appointed Gérant of the SARL with full powers to bind the company toward third parties, to open bank accounts, and to execute all documents necessary for the company's operations. This resolution takes immediate effect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Enshrine Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founders and their legal counsel; optional authentic act by a French Notaire if real estate or regulated in-kind contributions are involved.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Statuts in French, specifying the SARL legal form, corporate name, corporate purpose (software publishing and B2B enterprise SaaS), registered office address, share capital, class and distribution of quota parts, governance provisions, rights of gérant, and profit allocation rules. All shareholders must sign the final version; for a notarial act, each founder appears before the notary to execute with lawful identification.
required_dossiers: Copy of the office lease or ownership title for the registered office
Notarized powers of attorney for any signing representative
Identity documents of all shareholders and the designated gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or registry queries inconsistent statutory clauses, amend the Statuts by unanimous shareholder consent, re-sign the corrected pages, and resubmit. A refusal is cured by verifying the corporate purpose and capital rules before re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit Cash Capital and Obtain Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French licensed credit institution, Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, or a French notary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account (compte bancaire bloqué) in the name of the company being formed. Each shareholder wires or pays their cash contribution, with at least 20% paid up at the time of deposit. Request a Certificate of Capital Deposit (Attestation de dépôt des fonds) stating the depository institution, the total deposited amount, the company name, and the manager's authority to release funds upon RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of the shareholders and gérant
Beneficial ownership and simplified KYC declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires further AML/KYC clarifications, supply source-of-funds evidence and revised ownership declarations. If the institution refuses to open the account, select another bank or use a notary as statutory depositary; no reformation of the Statuts is needed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish a Legal Announcement in a Journal d'Annonces Légales
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) authorized by the Prefecture in the department of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pursuant to Article R.210-2 of the Commercial Code, issue a legal notice containing the proposed corporate name, legal form SARL, registered office address, corporate purpose, share capital, distribution of quota parts, and identity of the gérant. Publish the notice and obtain an Attestation de parution from the JAL within 15 days of registration of the filing request.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL queries typographical or statutory inconsistencies, revise the announcement text with the exact corporate details and republish; obtain a fresh Attestation de parution before filing with the Greffe.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Formation Application through Guichet Unique and Register with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique electronic portal, transmitted to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce having jurisdiction over the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form M0 in French, attach the signed Statuts, capital deposit certificate, publication attestation, registered office proof, identity documents, and the manager's statutory declaration. Pay the official filing fee by card or wire. The Greffe reviews legal consistency, performs identity checks, and issues the registration extract by adding the company to the RCS / RNE; the SIREN and SIRET numbers are generated by INSEE and transmitted automatically.
required_dossiers: Capital deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt des fonds)
Registered office title or lease consent
Identity document and criminal-record declaration of the gérant
Letter of acceptance of duties by the gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the dossier is rejected, review the Greffe’s reasoned notification within 30 days, correct all missing or defective documents, and resubmit through the Guichet unique. A second rejection may be appealed to the Prompt Decisions Judge (Juge Commissaire) of the competent Commercial Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Kbis Extract and Post-Registration Fiscal Identifiers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; INSEE; Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP); URSSAF.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, download the Extrait Kbis, which is the official company identity certificate. Confirm the APE/NAF code (6201Z) and the registered office address. The DGFiP automatically allocates a French VAT number (TVA intracommunautaire) for entities liable to French VAT unless a specific indication requires its activation; register any optional sector-specific identifier with the relevant administration (e.g., solely for insurance or banking if applicable).
required_dossiers: Notification of the gérant's identification number (SIREN)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis contains incorrect legal mentions, submit a rectification request to the Greffe. If the VAT number is not visible after registration, file a French EDI/EuVAT form or request issuance through the DGFiP business portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convene the Constitutive Governance Meeting and Finalize Internal Powers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders and the appointed Gérant; written minutes or private deed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the constitutive general assembly to approve the final Statuts, confirm the capital subscription and deposit, approve pre-registration acts (acts performed in the company's name), formally appoint the Gérant, and authorize the banking signatures of the gérant with sole or joint mandate. Record the session in written minutes; have all shareholders sign. If the Gérant is a legal entity, appoint its permanent representative in the same resolution.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the designated Gérant declines appointment after registration, an extraordinary shareholder meeting must be convened to replace the Gérant and to update the RCS via the relevant modification form. Failure to convene is cured by a subsequent unanimous written consent.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — ISIC 6201 (enterprise software/SaaS) is a non-industrial service activity; no manufacturing or physical production authorization is required.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required for B2B enterprise SaaS; the activity is exercised under the freedom of establishment. Only the ordinary business registration at the RCS/RNE is required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) / Ministère de la Transition Écologique, where an ICPE filing would otherwise apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category C registrations and full EIA reports do not apply because software development and hosted B2B solutions do not operate an installation classée pour la protection de l'environnement.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater discharge, volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions, or hazardous waste thresholds are triggered. General municipal waste collection rules and applicable data-center cooling standards (if a dedicated server room exists) remain subject to ordinary police/administrative conditions and to GDPR technical requirements only.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For the office occupier: valid fire safety certificate for any Établissement Recevant des Salariés (ERP type R) under the Labor Code; structural load confirmation for server racks or heavy equipment; electrical installation conformity certificate if a French electrical system is modified; compliance with the French Labor Code workplace hygiene, lighting, ventilation, and emergency exit requirements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des finances publiques (DGFiP), administered through the Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and the official portal impots.gouv.fr. Company formation and registration data are filed through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI); the Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques (INSEE) allocates the SIREN and SIRET identifiers.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate and register the SARL through the INPI Guichet unique. 2. Obtain the SIREN identifier for the legal entity and the SIRET identifier for each registered establishment from INSEE. 3. Open the entity's professional tax account on impots.gouv.fr and identify the competent SIE. 4. Submit the VAT registration request, normally using the applicable French VAT registration form and supporting corporate, business-activity, establishment, bank-account, and representative documentation. 5. The DGFiP issues or confirms the French VAT number in the format FR plus an administrative two-digit key and the entity's nine-digit SIREN. 6. Non-established entities making taxable supplies in France must register where required; a fiscal representative may be required for non-EU businesses, subject to applicable mutual-assistance rules. 7. Validate EU VAT numbers through the VIES system where intra-EU transactions are conducted. A French entity may have a SIREN without being VAT-registered if it qualifies for the French VAT exemption regime or has no taxable VAT activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SARL is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). There is no US-style check-the-box regime. Subject to statutory eligibility conditions, a SARL may elect taxation at shareholder level under the income tax regime: a qualifying newly established company may generally elect for a limited period of up to five fiscal years, while a qualifying family SARL may elect for income tax treatment without the ordinary five-year limitation. Elections are formal, generally irrevocable or subject to statutory withdrawal rules, and require timely notification to the relevant tax authority. French anti-hybrid-mismatch rules implementing ATAD 2 may deny deductions, impose inclusion, or neutralize mismatches; they do not constitute a freely available entity-classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: French value added tax (taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, or VAT), coordinated with the EU VAT Directive and customs rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no general turnover threshold that permits a non-established taxable person to ignore French VAT registration when it makes taxable supplies requiring registration in France. For French-established businesses, the domestic franchise en base de TVA exemption for services generally applies below the statutory annual turnover threshold of EUR 37,500, with a tolerance threshold of EUR 41,250 under applicable rules and annual legislative adjustments. A B2B SaaS supply to a business customer established in another EU Member State is generally subject to customer-accounted reverse charge and may require EU recapitulative reporting rather than French output VAT. The EU-wide EUR 10,000 threshold is relevant primarily to certain cross-border B2C electronic services and is separate from French domestic registration thresholds.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory domestic B2B electronic invoicing and transaction reporting. From 1 September 2026, all French-established businesses must be able to receive electronic invoices; issuance obligations apply from 1 September 2026 to large enterprises and intermediate-sized enterprises and from 1 September 2027 to small and medium-sized enterprises and micro-enterprises, subject to statutory transitional changes. Invoices must generally be transmitted through an accredited private platform or other authorized platform using prescribed structured formats and data fields. France uses a platform-based transmission and e-reporting model rather than universal real-time invoice clearance. E-reporting applies principally to qualifying transactions with non-established customers and certain payment data. Public-sector invoices continue to use the Chorus Pro framework. Digital archiving, invoice integrity, authenticity, readability, and audit-trail requirements apply.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from France or the EU to a destination outside the EU may be invoiced without French VAT if the supplier can prove export and customs exit in accordance with French and EU VAT rules. The supplier must retain the export declaration, the electronic customs exit result or equivalent exit evidence, commercial invoices, transport records, and transaction-level accounting support. B2B SaaS and other electronically supplied services are generally not treated as exported goods. A service supplied to a business customer established outside France is normally taxed according to the place-of-supply rule and may be outside the scope of French VAT or subject to reverse charge, rather than technically being a 0% export supply. The supplier must substantiate the customer's business status, establishment outside France, contractual supply location, and actual use where relevant. French VAT refunds require valid invoices, customs evidence where applicable, accounting records, and proof that input VAT relates to activities giving a right of deduction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export declaration and customs Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Electronic confirmation of exit from the EU customs territory or equivalent customs exit evidence
Commercial invoice identifying the exporter, customer, goods, value, delivery terms, and destination
Packing list and transport document, such as bill of lading, airway bill, or CMR consignment note, where applicable
Contract, purchase order, and accounting records linking the goods to the export transaction
Proof of delivery or destination evidence where required by the customs or tax audit
For services: customer VAT or business-identification evidence, contract, customer-establishment evidence, service description, place-of-supply analysis, and reverse-charge wording where applicable
Banking or payment records where relevant to commercial substantiation; an inward-remittance certificate is not generally a French statutory export-VAT document
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general foreign-exchange repatriation requirement or universal 180-day deadline for export proceeds. Export VAT exemption or deduction may be denied or clawed back if customs exit, customer status, destination, transport, or transaction records are insufficient. Reassessed VAT may include late-payment interest generally calculated at 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules, together with penalties commonly ranging from 10% for specified filing or payment failures to 40% for deliberate non-compliance and 80% for fraudulent maneuvers or abuse of rights. False documents, fraudulent VAT claims, or organized VAT fraud may trigger criminal prosecution, fines, and imprisonment under the French Tax Code and Penal Code. Customs violations may generate customs duties, VAT reassessment, fines, seizure, and loss of customs authorizations. The applicable assessment period and penalty depend on the nature of the error, concealment, fraud, and relevant limitation rules.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF) as central bank; Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor) under the Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty as the competent foreign exchange administrator and balance-of-payments reporting authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for both current-account and capital-account transactions under Articles 63–65 TFEU and the French Monetary and Financial Code (Articles L151-1 et seq.). No prior exchange-control license is required for profit remittances, dividend distributions, franchise royalties, or ordinary trade flows. Cross-border transfers to non-EEA destinations are subject only to statistical declaration obligations to the Banque de France and, for inbound direct investments capitalizing a French SARL, a mandatory ex-post or prior declaration under the FDI screening regime if the activity touches a sensitized sector (ordinary B2B SaaS activity is not sensitized). For outbound investments or capital account movements exceeding €1,000,000, DG Trésor reporting applies. SaaS revenue may be invoiced in foreign currencies, but statutory financial statements must be maintained in euros.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export-proceeds surrender deadline, mandatory conversion ratio, or obligation to repatriate foreign currency to a French concentrator account. Exporters may retain foreign currency in domiciled bank accounts established in France, provided each transaction or periodic aggregation exceeds the €750,000 monthly balance-of-payments reporting threshold and the corresponding declaration is filed with the Banque de France. Receipts may be freely converted, offset against foreign-currency payables, or used for treasury operations without central-bank authorization.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for payment routing, low feasibility as a sole banking relationship. French-approved or passporting Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) such as Wise, Revolut, Payoneer, and Qonto provide remote onboarding, multi-currency IBANs, and lower-cost cross-border execution. They are authorized under PSD2 and may receive third-party SaaS subscription payments in multiple currencies. However, an EMI account is not a deposit account; funds are safeguarded, not covered by the French statutory deposit-guarantee scheme. A capital contribution to a new SARL is safer through a full-service conventional bank. For operational use, combining a tier-1 bank for treasury and borrowing with an EMI for cross-border payables is viable and legally compliant.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French banks systematically require physical presentation of each director (or duly registered co-gérant) and the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) when opening a professional corporate account. Video-identification is permitted under Article R561-10-1 of the Monetary and Financial Code, but many commercial banks still require an in-person appointment to validate the corporate statute, the UBO declarations, and the source of funds. In practice, at least one natural-person director with signing power must appear at the branch or receive a visiting corporate KYC officer. Remote opening is occasionally accepted when the KYC file is prepared by an established French intermediate or attorney.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder or UBO of a French SARL
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original or certified extract from the foreign company registry; current international passport and proof of residential address for the natural-person UBO; audited financial statements or tax return substantiating the source of wealth; a funding-chain confirmation letter from the client's existing bank; a board resolution explicitly endorsing the French entity's capital contribution; and a sworn statement that the contributed funds are unencumbered and derived from lawful commercial activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border SaaS invoice trail with high incoming transaction velocity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed master subscription agreements, standard terms-of-service linked to a published website, purchase orders from distinct enterprise customers, treasury-consolidated payment reconciliation report, and a copy of the VAT registration certificate proving a French taxable personality. In addition, a company presentation package explaining the low-risk recurring-revenue nature of the software-as-a-service model and a commitment to provide transaction-level explanations on AML request.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Receipts from jurisdictions under enhanced-AML scrutiny or high-risk money-laundering jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A jurisdiction-specific risk assessment prepared by the MLRO or external advisory firm; commercial contracts involving local distributors data-centre providers or resellers; proof of economic substance in the counterparts (registered address, business license); and confirmation that each transaction is settled through an already-KYC cleared correspondent bank. For particularly challenged jurisdictions, a six-month telemetric analysis of user behaviour and revenue cycle supports the legitimate-end-activity defence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained quick switch of the treasury account or concentration of recurring subscription payments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A bank-switching certificate issued by the previous account-holder within the French banking system (demande de mobilité bancaire), audited annual accounts, historical cash-flow waterfall, and the external auditor's comfort letter acknowledging revenue-recognition policies in accordance with IFRS 15. This bundle neutralises the red flag by demonstrating predictable commercial use.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a capital contribution from a non-French shareholder, the standard compliant routing is a SWIFT MT103 wire from the shareholder's retained bank account to the SARL's tier-1 Paris-based euro operating account. The wire must include a structured reference identifying the investor, the corporate name (FR SARL), and the transaction purpose code 'S13 / Direct Investment Capital Contribution'. A Unique End-to-End Transaction Reference (UETR) shall be recorded. The bank will require a copy of the executed board/partner resolution showing the authorised subscription, a statement of the amount and currency of issuance of capital, and evidence of the beneficial-owner identification. If the inbound amount corresponds to registered capital, contribution must occur no later than the statutory deadline and be verified by the managing director. For amounts exceeding the €750,000 threshold, a balance-of-payments declaration to Banque de France and a mandatory FDI declaration to DG Trésor via its dedicated portal are required; the declarations are ex-post except where the shareholder participates in actions listed in Article R151-3 of the Monetary and Financial Code, in which case prior authorization is necessary.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Cross-border disbursements for trade creditors, cloud-infrastructure providers, overseas distributors, and intercompany service fees shall be executed via secure clearing rails as follows: (1) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) in euro for EEA counterparties; (2) SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA euro and foreign-currency payments, including required structured beneficiary identifiers and invoice references; (3) ISO 20022 MX pain.001 for batch enterprise payments when integrated with a treasury workstation; (4) commercial letters of credit or standby letters of credit only where a contractual guarantee is mandatory, typically for procurement of hardware from Asia; (5) first-party open-loop corporate cards (Virtual Business Credit Cards) for small-value digital-advertising and software-license payments; and (6) EMI rails such as Wise Business for rapid multi-currency settlement where the counterparty is not a sanctioned entity and the beneficial recipient is identifiably the contracted supplier. Treasury must archive proof of the underlying commercial invoice and proof of FX execution in the compliance dossier, as French banking counterparties may request transactional evidence up to five years after execution.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla foreign-exchange forward contracts (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF)
FX swaps (cross-currency swaps) for converting surplus EUR into operational currencies and reversing at maturity
Zero-premium collars to cap EUR/USD volatility on future subscription revenue
Euro-dollar commercial paper swaps to hedge multi-currency liquidity positions
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on emerging-market currencies (e.g., INR, CNY) where onshore access is restricted, subject to bank counterparty ISDA/EMIR documentation
Currency options (put/call strategies) to protect against adverse translation of significant international-sales receivables
Cross-currency interest rate swaps where the SARL holds a euro-denominated debt but receives a contractual cash flow in foreign currency

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual filing of financial statements (bilan and compte de résultat)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 15th day of the 4th month after fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties of 0.1% of turnover per month of delay, capped at 5% of turnover; non-filing may result in administrative fines and potential dissolution

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if SARL exceeds two of: turnover >800,000 EUR, total assets >400,000 EUR, or >50 employees

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual update and confirmation of Ultimate Beneficial Owners and shareholding in Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 0 - 2,000 USD (mandatory registered office or professional registered agent)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard rate of impôt sur les sociétés (IS) applicable since 1 January 2022; reduced 15% rate applies to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for qualifying small businesses with fiscal-year revenue not exceeding EUR 10 million and fully paid-up capital.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Jeune Entreprise Innovante (JEI): 100% IS exemption for the first profitable accounting period and 50% for the following period, subject to company age under 8 years and R&D expenses at least 15% of tax-deductible charges; Crédit d'Impôt Recherche (CIR): 30% tax credit on eligible R&D expenditure up to EUR 100 million and 5% above; Crédit d'Impôt Innovation (CII) for SMEs at 20% of eligible innovation expenses up to EUR 400,000; parent-subsidiary regime (régime des sociétés mères) exempting qualifying dividend income; one-year deficit carry-back of up to EUR 1,000,000 credited against future corporate tax.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carry-forward (correcting the template default of 5): under Article 209 CGI, losses are offset indefinitely against future profits subject to the annual cap of EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the taxable profit exceeding EUR 1,000,000; a one-year carry-back of up to EUR 1,000,000 is also available.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 (liasse fiscale 2065 and schedules 2050-2059) filed electronically through EFI (Espace Fiscal Entreprises) on impots.gouv.fr using the PISTE/teleTVA protocol; dividend and withholding tax reconciliations reported on Forms 2561 (relevé de dividendes) and 2777 (levy on income from movable assets).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual / Quarterly: annual IS return plus quarterly prepayments (acomptes) due 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December, with the final balance (solde) settled at filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the fiscal year-end (Article 223 CGI); e-filing extends the deadline by 15 days. For a 31 December year-end, the filing deadline is 3 May (paper) or 17 May (electronic); for other fiscal year-ends, the deadline is the end of the third month following the close (electronic filers obtain a 15-day extension).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box A - Désignation de la société (page 1, Form 2065)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identity: SIREN number, NAF/APE code 6201Z (computer programming), legal form SARL, registered office, fiscal year dates and principal establishment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify non-resident shareholders and file Form 2561 to report all foreign payouts; avoid any factual indication of a permanent establishment through French-based servers, staff or support functions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Table 2052, line AI - Résultat fiscal imposable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable profit at the 25% rate: accounting profit after add-backs of non-deductible expenses (penalties, excess depreciation, 40% of mixed vehicle costs, non-deductible taxes) and after deduction of prior-year deficit set-offs and tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile intercompany SaaS revenue and licence fees: every intra-group transaction must be priced at arm's length under Article 57 CGI with contemporaneous documentation, otherwise the deduction is denied on audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Table 2052, line BI - Résultat soumis au taux réduit de 15%
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: First EUR 42,500 of eligible profit subject to the reduced 15% rate; eligibility requires annual turnover below EUR 10 million and at least 75% of capital held by natural persons or qualifying SMEs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify the ownership test when capital is held by a foreign corporate parent; a corporate-parent-owned SARL generally fails the reduced-rate condition unless the parent itself qualifies as an SME under EU Annex I Recommendation 2003/361/EC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of tax losses brought forward and set off in the current year, computed under Article 209 CGI with the EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of excess limitation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain loss-versus-substance evidence: abuse-of-law challenge (Article L. 64 LPF) may recharacterize artificial losses allocated to France when SaaS operations are managed and controlled by non-resident directors.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Table 2058-A - Produits financiers et retenues à la source
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial income, foreign-source royalties, interest and French withholding taxes eligible for imputation as tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare all software licensing royalties received from French clients; royalties paid out to non-resident IP owners remain subject to the 33.33% withholding mechanism unless EU Directive or treaty relief applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation and imputation of CIR at 30% of eligible R&D expenses (up to EUR 100 million; 5% above) for software development and prototypes; unused credit is reimbursable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident freelance developers do not count as French CIR-eligible payroll; document IP ownership and technical subcontracting to defend the credit in a research audit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or omitted Form 2065: 10% surcharge if filed within 30 days of formal notice, 40% for deliberate non-filing, 80% for fraudulent maneuvers; automatic late-payment interest of 0.20% per month (2.4% p.a.); EUR 150 minimum fine per missing schedule; a false tax return triggers Article 1741 CGI criminal exposure of up to EUR 500,000 and 5 years' imprisonment.
